notes: DS-GEN-18 STALLED's own corpus fallback line contains a semicolon, which breaches the mechanical bar the brief itself enforces (no semicolon); per the brief's own rule not to imitate a corpus breach, I wrote a fresh two-sentence spine instead of copying it verbatim.
DS-ECO-1 COMBINATION C3's corpus line uses a colon, which PART V of the brief lists as a device the fair copy does not have (notebook-only); avoided it in my own version for the same reason.

Two stance values in the turn ("threshold" on PRESSURED, "counterforce" on TIER: minor shadow activity) are not among the brief's three defined stances (ledger/street/visitor), so their intended effect on the prose beyond a flavor tag was unclear.

DS-ECO-9 PRESSURED instructs writing exactly one sentence and no second, but its own corpus fallback is two sentences -- a direct contradiction between the card's instruction and the fallback it supplies. I followed the one-sentence instruction.

DS-ECO-12 INCOME MIX's pool title says "two or three sources between them" but the field data given is economicState.incomeSources.length = 10 (not marked UNREADABLE the way other engine-decided fields are); unclear whether "two or three" or the length of 10 is authoritative, so I asserted no specific count either way.

The `stance` label on each pool (visitor / street / ledger / threshold / counterforce) is given but the brief only says the three old stances survive as 'the spine line's tag', and 'threshold' and 'counterforce' are not among them (ledger/street/visitor). With faces:0 everywhere, it was unclear whether a stance is supposed to shape the bare spine at all, so I wrote all spines as the archiver's bare fact per ruling 40 and the SHAPE-OF-WHAT-YOU-RETURN section.

Two corpus lines break bars the brief declares hard, and the brief says to keep the CLAIM but not imitate the breach — leaving the claim itself unusable in one case. DS-ECO-6's corpus asserts 'nothing organised behind it', which the brief's own floor-1 example names as refused on a town whose rows list a street gang and front businesses, and this town lists both. I kept the 'minor' reading and dropped the 'nothing organised' claim; if the corpus claim is mandatory, that pool is unwritable.

The 'second sentence must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' rule collides with pools whose only fields are 'UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD' (DS-ECO-1, DS-ECO-10, DS-GEN-18). There is no lawful second sentence available there, which is not stated; I wrote one sentence in each. Similarly DS-ECO-12's INCOME MIX key says 'two or three sources between them' while the field reads a length of ten, so the key and the field disagree and no digit may be written either way.

The dm-only pool (DS-ECO-6) says the private note 'still rides in `spine`' and that `notebook` is none, so the schema's notebook array is empty on the one unit that is actually a notebook entry. That is internally consistent but inverts the audience rule stated in the brief's DM REGISTER section, which says notebook carries the private rows on audience dm.

Slot guidance is permissive ('slots you may use') with no instruction on whether an offered slot must appear. Four pools offer {settlement}, but the page-level bar allows the name at most once per unit and never as the first word of two units, so I spent it once, mid-sentence, and wrote around it elsewhere. Whether an unused slot counts against the unit is not said.

Page is audience dm, but every one of the 17 pools says 'faces to write: 0' and 'notebook: none'. So the whole DM register (PART V) and the entire face machinery of the brief (sources, pairs, weighings, compromised roles, one face per seated source) has nothing to act on here; the tab is spine-only and the brief's longest sections were inapplicable.

Nearly every pool's fields read 'UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD', while the rule states a second sentence must rest on one of those fields and name it in its own word. That makes a lawful second sentence effectively impossible in most pools, so I wrote one sentence throughout; it is unclear whether one-sentence spines are the intent or a degenerate outcome.

Several corpus lines break bars they are given under: MARKET-OPEN states an origin (a founding-as-record, explicitly refused), three spines use semicolons and one a colon, and the foodSecurity line's closing 'which it is not in a comfortable town' contradicts the page's own prosperity badge 'Comfortable' and is also a which-clause close. I kept each claim and dropped the breach, but the instruction 'the claim you must keep' is hard to honour when the claim itself is the barred element.

Two pools on one page pull opposite ways with no guidance: DS-GEN-5 'ordinary' claims the town takes very little from the road, DS-GEN-6 'road' claims the road is a condition of the town's existence. I wrote them as through-traffic versus inbound supply so they can stand together, but the reconciliation was mine to invent.

Two smaller gaps. The stance words used here (elder, unfolding, counterforce, 'ledger · marks deficit') are never defined in the brief, which names only ledger/street/visitor. And the scores.magical WEAK claim ('no arrangement for magic') sits against the page's own arrival scene (a magelight lamp post at the gate) and the card's Alchemist shop, with no statement of whether that counts as a contradicted page line.

Seats with no roster: DS-DEF-2 'Invasion & War' face 0 is seated on `elders` and the two DS-DEF-2 faces seated on `garrison` have no entry under the town's `roles`/`sources`. I followed the 'copy the corpus verbatim at that seat' rule. For `elders` that forces a contradiction: the corpus row still carries unfilled `{elders}` and `{v:take}` tokens, and the pool declares no slots, so a verbatim copy prints raw identifiers, which the mechanical bars forbid. No rule says which one wins.

Slot declarations disagree with themselves in 'Invasion & War': the pool says 'slots you may use: (none)' and then declares a `{court}` fill. I wrote a court role in plain words and used no token. Also unclear whether a declared fill must be spent or may be skipped for {settlement}; I read it as optional and named the town in one unit only, to respect the once-per-page opening rule.

The brief's attribution guidance is self-contradictory on one frame: 'one of the aldermen has it that' is offered as licensed syntax variation while 'has it that' is listed among the mannered frames ruling 42 struck. I avoided the frame entirely.

'The second sentence of a unit must rest on one of these fields' is ambiguous against the three-sentence unit cap, since a rendered unit is spine plus a drawn face. I kept nearly every spine and face to one sentence so no combination exceeds three, which may under-use the licence.

Two roster roles collide with ruling 42c's plain-word bar: the stranger roster seats 'a pedlar' and the register roster 'the high priest' / class language the bar rewrites. I avoided 'pedlar'. Also, 'granary' is an institution row name but a barred word, so I wrote 'grain store' throughout.
